GB.headline: The strongest winds from Storm Boelo are expected Saturday evening and Sunday morning.
GB.description:
Very strong westerly winds associated with Storm Boelo are expected with fairly widespread gusts of 60 to 70 mph and gusts to 80 mph in exposed coastal areas. While strong winds are expected across a wider area with a yellow warning in force, there is higher confidence in impacts and disruption taking place within this amber warning area. The winds will gradually ease from the west during Sunday morning. 

This is an update to the amber warning already in force, as Northern Ireland will see the wind easing earlier than other parts of the UK. 

For further details see https://www.metoffice.gov.

GB.headline: Heavy rain brings a high likelihood of moderate impacts from surface water flooding.
GB.description:
Heavy rain in association with Storm Boelo is expected to lead to surface water flooding in places. 25-30mm is expected widely across the warning area during this time, with a few places such as upland areas seeing 50-60mm, and some of this perhaps falling within 6 hours. Rain will ease for a time through the evening, but this will be followed by another intense band of heavy rain following in from the west, before the whole system clears away eastward to bring a clear night with a few scattered showers following on.

For further details see https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/weather/warnings-and-ad

GB.headline: Heavy rain associated with Storm Boelo is likely to cause some travel disruption and flooding in a few places
GB.description:
Frequent heavy showers or more organised bands of rain will develop across northern Scotland during Saturday evening in association with Storm Boelo, continuing through Sunday morning and early afternoon. 

Accumulations of 20-40 mm are expected widely within the warning area through this period, with 60-80 mm possible in some locations, bringing flooding and travel disruption in a few places. Showers will become less frequent later through Sunday afternoon.

For further details see https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/weather/warnings-and-advice/uk-warnings
areas: Central, Tayside & Fife | Grampian | Highlands & Eilean Siar

GB.headline: A period of strong winds may lead to damaging gusts and transport disruption.
GB.description:
Strong west to southwesterly winds are expected to spread across much of Scotland, the north of Northern Ireland and northern England on Tuesday. Gusts of 50-60 mph are possible quite widely and some coastal or exposed areas could see gusts of 70 mph or more, but at this time there is some uncertainty in where, and how strong, the peak gusts will be. The strongest of the winds will reduce from the southwest later on Tuesday, with the far north of Scotland the last to see winds ease.



For further details see https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/weather/warnings-and-advice/uk-warnings
